name: Coconut-heart salad
summary: Củ hủ dừa is a light salad of coconut heart, white and mildly sweet. The prawn-and-pork plate adds tiger prawn, pork belly, laksa leaf, roasted peanut, fried shallot, and carrot in a lime-and-sugar dressing.
origin: The grove lunch on Vietnam Tourism, and guest tables on the provincial tourism site.
culture: The 4 June 2021 article says this salad and rice steamed in a coconut were named among 100 Vietnamese dishes for 2011–2016 by Vietkings. That is the site’s account. The article says the salad is a guest dish, including weddings, death anniversaries, and full-month feasts. It also says some palms are grown for the heart, so the cut is not only a felled crop tree.
texture: The site says the prawn is crisp and the pork belly is rich, against the white heart. Soak the cut heart in cold water with a little lime juice so it stays white.
taste: The site calls the heart mildly sweet and cool, and the finished salad sour-sweet, rich, and easy. Vietnam Tourism calls it a light salad and does not give a dressing.
howToEat: Vietnam Tourism: eat the light salad at the grove lunch with the coconut rice and the coconut-braised shrimp.

The 4 June 2021 method: cut the heart into short strips, boil the prawns and the pork belly, slice the pork and the carrot, and toss with laksa leaf in a lime-and-sugar dressing. Finish with roasted peanut and fried shallot. The article says garlic-chili fish sauce and a shrimp cracker on the side. That cracker is not bánh phồng Sơn Đốc.
where: Tourism stops and guest tables. Vietnam Tourism puts the salad on the grove lunch.
seoTitle: Coconut-heart salad in Ben Tre — two accounts
seoDescription: Củ hủ dừa is a light salad of coconut heart, white and mildly sweet, or a prawn-and-pork gỏi in a lime-and-sugar dressing.
